claims.text: The platinum-group nanoscale catalyst exhibits high activity for ethanol oxidation under steady-state electrochemical conditions.
The catalyst exhibits high selectivity for ethanol oxidation.
The catalyst exhibits high durability during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamic formation and modulation of surface oxide/hydroxide species governs the catalyst's ethanol-oxidation performance.
Periodic potential shifts above and below the oxide-formation threshold modulate surface oxide/hydroxide coverage.
Elevated potentials promote formation of surface oxide/hydroxide species.
Dynamic surface oxide/hydroxide species alter the local electronic structure of the platinum-group metal surface.
The oxide/hydroxide-induced electronic-state change enhances adsorption of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The altered adsorption of intermediates promotes a 12-electron/12-proton ethanol-oxidation pathway.
Reducing the applied potential partially reduces the surface oxide/hydroxide species.
Partial reduction of the surface oxide/hydroxide species moderates catalytic activity.
Cycling between surface oxidation and reduction balances catalytic activity and durability.
Oxide/hydroxide coverage correlates with ethanol-oxidation current density.
Promoting dynamic oxide/hydroxide formation increases ethanol-oxidation current density relative to oxide-suppressed operation.
Promoting dynamic oxide/hydroxide formation improves selectivity toward complete ethanol-oxidation products.
Promoting dynamic oxide/hydroxide formation improves durability during extended operation.
A stable, non-dynamic oxide layer can passivate the catalyst and invalidate the proposed dynamic-oxide mechanism.
The mechanism may not govern performance at extreme pH or in non-aqueous solvents where oxide/hydroxide dynamics are not dominant.
